title: The CAP Theorem and the Limits of Distributed Consistency
explainer: Any multi-cloud or hybrid architecture that replicates data across regions or providers runs into the trade-off formalized as the CAP theorem: a distributed system cannot simultaneously guarantee full consistency, availability, and tolerance of network partitions. Eric Brewer proposed this as a conjecture around 2000, and Seth Gilbert and Nancy Lynch gave it a formal proof in 2002. Understanding CAP explains why real multi-cloud systems explicitly choose which guarantee to relax rather than promising all three at once.
